7.0.0.en: The building of the Temple of the Lord took seven years, while Solomon built his palace in 13 years. The number seven symbolizes perfection, for God rested on the seventh day of the creation of the world, and Solomon built the Temple with all perfection and precision. The speed of the building of the Temple compared with the time taken to build his palace is due to the fact that King David had prepared much for the building of the Temple, and also that the area of Solomon's own dwelling was larger than the area of the Temple, in addition to the fact that Solomon's concern was to build the house of God before his own house, so he mustered for it a huge number of workers who worked with energy and great joy for God. They were worn out in building the house of the Lord, so their number became smaller and their energy also less. For all this, the building of Solomon's palace, or his houses, took more time than the time of building the Temple.

7.0.1.en: What is meant by Solomon's house is a group of houses connected to one another for his dwelling and for administrative work and military preparations, in addition to a house for women, that is, the house of Pharaoh's daughter.

7.0.2.en: Solomon spent three years in preparing for the building of the Temple, then seven years in building it, and thirteen years in building his house on the hill called Zion, and after that he had only seventeen years left to manage his affairs in his palaces. After that he turned his attention to trade and to acquiring horses, chariots, and many marriages, and this was at the expense of his care for raising his many sons, and this appeared in his son Rehoboam, who was not wise, so that the kingdom was split at the beginning of his reign.

7.1.0.en: The forest of Lebanon: the forests of Lebanon.

7.1.2.en: Solomon built his houses south of the Temple on the same mountain on which the Temple was built, which is called Mount Zion, or Mount Moriah, or the city of David, and he describes in detail the first of these buildings, which is called the house of the forest of Lebanon. It is a building about 50 meters long, 25 meters wide, and fifteen meters high. It was called the forest of Lebanon because the timber used in its construction was cedar of Lebanon. Its roof was built of beams, that is, long timbers of cedar wood, and these beams, or cross-beams, rested on four rows of columns made of cedar wood, across the width of the building, which is twenty-five meters, and the rows extend the length of the building, which is fifty meters, with a large number of columns, the number of which is not mentioned.

7.2.1.en: The house of the forest of Lebanon contained 45 rooms divided among three stories, that is, each story contained fifteen rooms. The rooms of each story were divided as follows: six rooms along each side of the house lengthwise and three rooms across its width, and the roofs of all the rooms were of cedar wood. The rooms were distributed along three sides of the hall, and the fourth side is the entrance, that is, in the shape of the letter U, and all the rooms look out onto the hall.

7.2.2.en: In each room there was a window looking out on the outer courtyard, with another window in the same room opposite it looking out on the inner hall of the house, and the windows of the rooms on the right side of the house faced and were in line with the windows in the rooms on the left side of the house. The windows in the three stories were one above the other on a single line. All this gives good ventilation and lighting to the rooms and the inner hall. The house of the forest of Lebanon is the administrative building, through which Solomon managed the affairs of the kingdom using its many rooms, in addition to its being storehouses for weapons.

7.3.0.en: Square: that is, its upper surface straight and not round in the shape of an arch.

7.3.1.en: Covered: that is, the upper lintel, which is the upper frame of the door, whose width is the thickness of the wall, so that the thickness of the wall becomes a roof for the door.

7.3.2.en: He describes the doors of the house as square, with wooden posts on both sides of the door in which the leaves are fixed, and the width of the roof of the door was the thickness of the wall. He emphasizes here that the windows were one above the other in the three stories.

7.4.0.en: A porch of pillars: a hall that is the entrance of the building, roofed and resting on columns.

7.4.1.en: Thresholds: plural of threshold, which is the upper or lower lintel, and what is meant here is the lower lintel. There was a hall called the hall of pillars because of the many columns in it, about 25 meters long and about 15 meters wide, and in front of it was another hall, also with columns, and at the end of the second hall were several steps (a stair). The second hall was prepared here to be an entrance to the third porch, in which Solomon's throne was placed (v. 7). Neither the porch of pillars nor the other porch in front of it had walls, but columns bearing a roof, and all of it was made of cedar wood.

7.5.0.en: Solomon made a porch, that is, a hall with three walls and an entrance on the fourth side, and it was called the porch of the throne, that is, Solomon's throne, where he sat upon it to judge the various affairs of the kingdom. He covered the walls of the hall from the floor to the roof with cedar wood. He made this porch splendid, with walls covered with precious timber, to befit the king's council.

7.5.1.en: It is understood from the above that Solomon made a hall with columns, the porch of pillars, and this hall leads to another hall which also has columns, and at the end of this other hall there are several steps (a stair) leading to the porch of the throne or of judgment, where Solomon sits to judge.

7.6.0.en: Solomon built a house for his dwelling in front of the porch of judgment and connected to it, so there is no separation between the porch of judgment and the king's palace. He also built a house next to it for the residence of Pharaoh's daughter, which is the house of the women. The Temple was to the north of these houses. The building of Solomon's house and the house of Pharaoh's daughter was like the building of the house of the forest of Lebanon and the porch of judgment, that is, with the same kind of stones and timber.

7.6.1.en: Solomon's care in building a house for the women or for Pharaoh's daughter is a type of Christ, who took care to build a house for His bride, that is, the Church, and also of His receiving the Gentiles with the Jews.

7.6.2.en: There was the great court (v. 9), which surrounds all these buildings, that is, the house of the forest of Lebanon and the three porches, that is, the porch of pillars, the other porch, and the porch of the throne, then Solomon's house, the house of the women, and the Temple. It is also called the outer court, or the great court; that is, it is a large courtyard surrounded by a wall, and inside it all the preceding buildings.

7.6.3.en: Within the great court there is another court, which is the middle court, and it surrounds Solomon's house and the house of Pharaoh's daughter (the house of the women). After the middle court is the inner court, which surrounds the Temple, the court of the priests, and the court of the people (see the drawing of Solomon's buildings at the end of the book).

7.7.0.en: The cornice: the top of the wall next to the roof.

7.7.1.en: Solomon took care to build all these preceding buildings of large stones, not cut with axes but with special saws so that they were even on all sides, and he covered them with cedar wood, with complete precision.

7.8.0.en: Solomon also took care in building the foundations of these buildings, which were huge stones four or five meters long, and they were good, the same stones that were used in the rest of the building, and so the buildings were founded in a good manner to rise to enormous heights with the utmost safety.

7.8.1.en: This shows Solomon as a type of Christ, who builds His house, that is, the Church, which is also His body, with all precision by the work of His Holy Spirit and founded on His precious blood shed on the wood of the Cross.

7.8.2.en: Take care of the foundation of your life, that is, your faith in God and your holding fast to the Church and its sacraments, so that you have a strong spiritual building, virtues, and good relationships, and are successful with people as long as you are strong in your relationship with God.

7.9.0.en: The huge stones used in the walls were also hewn according to specified measurements and were covered with boards of cedar wood.

7.10.0.en: The porch of the house: that is, the porch of the house of the Lord.

7.10.1.en: The great court that surrounds all these buildings had its walls formed of three rows of hewn stones covered with boards of cedar wood in a manner similar to the inner court that surrounds the Temple, and likewise the middle court that surrounds Solomon's house and the house of Pharaoh's daughter (the house of the women); that is, the stones are laid one above another in the building of the wall and covered on top with blocks of cedar wood to protect them, bind them, and fasten them.

7.11.s.en: (2) Hiram makes the bronze components of the Temple

7.11.0.en: Solomon summoned from Tyre one of the most skilled workers in bronze, Hiram, the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, whose father was a Gentile. He had wide experience and complete understanding of the manufacture of bronze things, so he came to Solomon and did all the work that Solomon assigned to him. Perhaps, because his mother was a Jewess, Hiram took care to complete the works assigned to him with precision. This Hiram is different from Hiram king of Tyre.

7.11.1.en: God allowed this man of Gentile origin to work in His house, and this signifies that Christ is coming to save the Jews and the Gentiles. So know that God seeks the salvation of all, and do not despise anyone, however far away he is or however many his sins, for Christ seeks the salvation of the whole world.

7.12.s.en: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

7.12.1.en: The other: that is, the one pillar.

7.12.2.en: Solomon made two pillars and set them up before the Holy Place in the porch of the Temple (v. 21); the two pillars do not bear a roof but were made to adorn the Temple. He made them of bronze, and the length of each was nine meters and its circumference six meters. The pillar was hollow, and the thickness of its wall, that is, the thickness of the bronze it was made of, was four fingers (Jer 52:21), and the Book of Chronicles tells us that each pillar had a base four meters high (2 Chr 3:15).

7.13.0.en: To show the greatness of the pillar and the greatness of the Temple in which it stood, he made for each pillar a capital of spherical shape. The height of the capital was two and a half meters, and this capital was also made of bronze.

7.14.0.en: A network of bronze was made, and on it seven wreaths, also of bronze, to adorn the capital.

7.15.0.en: He made for the capital two rows of bronze globes in the form of pomegranates, and the number of these pomegranates was a hundred in each row. Each pillar had two rows of pomegranates on the edges of the upper and lower networks, as also appears from (v. 42). That is, the base of the pillar bears a cylinder, and above the cylinder is a round row of pomegranates, and above it the ball of the capital, and on it the network on which are the wreaths, and above the capital a second round row of pomegranates, then the lily flower at the top of the pillar. So the base has the pillar above it, then the capital, then the lily flower.

7.16.0.en: Of molten brass: the shape of the lily cast and formed of bronze.

7.16.1.en: He made above the capital the shape of a lily flower, which resembles the lotus flower. When it says in this verse "as in the porch," it means that the flowers carved on the door of the Holy Place, which are seen in the porch, were some of them in the shape of the lily flower (ch. 6:18). The height of the lily flower above the capital was two meters. The lily shape symbolizes purity and holiness, since Christ is likened in the Song of Songs to this flower (Song 2:1).

7.17.0.en: It confirms here that the shape of the two capitals on the two pillars was the same.

7.18.0.en: After he finished the two pillars, he set them up in the porch of the Temple and called one of them "Jachin," that is, Jehovah establishes or makes firm, and called the other pillar "Boaz," that is, Jehovah is mighty. It is clear from the height of the two pillars that they did not bear the roof of the house but were placed before the house for adornment and for spiritual meanings, which are:

7.18.1.en: 1- The believer ought to be firm in the Church like the pillar, never moving, because salvation is within the Church and steadfastness is necessary for salvation.

7.18.2.en: 2- By the believer's steadfastness within the house of God, he receives glory and might before God on earth and in heaven, as the two pillars were named Jachin and Boaz.

7.18.3.en: 3- God rejoices in His children in His Church, for they adorn it with their prayers, like these two pillars adorned with the two capitals and the two flowers.

7.18.4.en: 4- The believer ought to be adorned with virtues, which are symbolized by the pomegranates that cover the pillar and rise above it.

7.18.5.en: 5- These two pillars were made of bronze, which is a symbol of spiritual striving on earth, and therefore the two pillars were placed in the porch, and when a person completes his striving he reaches the Kingdom of Heaven, where there are gold and the angels, that is, the cherubim, and this is what the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies symbolize.

7.18.6.en: 6- God commanded the setting up of the pillars before the Holy Place because God is the One who sets up and establishes the believer by His grace in the house of the Lord.

7.18.7.en: 7- The two pillars are a type of God's leading of His people, as He used to lead them in the wilderness by the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night.

7.18.8.en: 8- The capital in the form of a network symbolizes the believers' concern for catching souls and drawing them to the Church.

7.18.9.en: 9- The pomegranate, whose taste is sharp, symbolizes spiritual striving, and its red color on the inside symbolizes the blood of Christ the Redeemer; that is, the pomegranate symbolizes the grace of Christ the Savior, who supports His striving children.

7.18.10.en: 10- The two pillars are tall, so they symbolize the believer, who is a light to the world and shines like bronze, giving light to others and drawing others to God.

7.18.11.en: I wish that you would be steadfast in the sacraments of the Church and all its spiritual practices, so that you are adorned with many virtues and so do your work without knowing it, influencing those around you as they see Christ in you and love Him because of your spiritual conduct among them.

7.19.0.en: A line of thirty cubits did compass it round about: the circumference of the sea was 30 cubits, that is, about 15 meters.

7.19.1.en: He made a large basin of bronze for the priests to wash in, and called it the sea because of its large size compared with the laver that was in the tabernacle of meeting. This sea was round in shape, its upper mouth wider than its base, and its mouth in the form of a circle whose diameter was ten cubits, that is, five meters, and whose circumference was thirty cubits, that is, fifteen meters, and the height of the brim of this basin from the ground was five cubits, that is, two and a half meters.

7.20.0.en: He adorned the sea with two rows of gourd shapes, ten gourds to a cubit, and these two rows were under the brim of the sea, all made of bronze and cast of it. They symbolize the spiritual fruits with which the priest ought to be adorned, who washes in the water of the sea, as a sign of the purity with which he is clothed, in order to be able to carry out his service inside the house of the Lord, that is, the Holy Place.

7.21.0.en: Their hinder parts: the rear of their bodies.

7.21.1.en: He made the sea rest on 12 oxen made and cast of bronze, three oxen on each of the four sides, with their faces outward and their hinder parts inward, so the observer sees the faces of the oxen. The twelve oxen are a type of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, for the priest enters the Holy Place after he is purified in the sea, to be a representative of all the believers in the service of God, that is, a representative of the twelve tribes. The twelve oxen are also a type of the twelve Apostles, by whom the world was preached to concerning the salvation of Christ, repentance, and Baptism. The faces of the oxen are outward so that the oxen, distinguished by strength, appear as a proclamation of the power of the priesthood.

7.21.2.en: Because the priests wash in the sea, it is a type of Baptism and repentance, by which we are able to stand before God; the ox is also a type of the sacrifice of Christ, and the blood of Christ is the foundation of salvation and the sacraments. The faces of the oxen are turned toward the four directions, three on each side, and the number three symbolizes the Holy Trinity, whom the Apostles preached in the four quarters of the world.

7.22.0.en: Bath: a measure for liquids equal to approximately 23 liters.

7.22.2.en: The sea, which was in the shape of a basin, had a brim like the brim of the cup from which a person drinks, and the thickness of the wall of the sea was a handbreadth, that is, about 20 cm. Perhaps this brim was suitable for the priest to sit on when he goes up to the sea and goes down into it, and perhaps Solomon made a set of ladders or steps by which the priests went up or down inside the sea to wash, and the capacity of the basin was two thousand baths.

7.22.3.en: God in His love welcomes you greatly in His Church, but at the same time He is a great and awesome God. So you ought to be purified by repentance and confession, in order to be able to stand before Him and partake of His mysteries and enjoy fellowship with Him and His tenderness.

7.23.0.en: After that he made ten movable lavers (v. 38) on ten square bases, their length equal to their width, each of them two meters, and their height a meter and a half. These lavers were used to wash the flesh of the sacrifices (2 Chr 4:6).

7.24.1.en: Ledges: plural of ledge, which is the frame or border in which the panel is set.

7.24.2.en: The base was a square bronze board with a frame surrounding it, cast with it as one piece, and on this board and its frame were shapes of lions, oxen, and cherubim. From the four sides of the frame hung bronze wreaths of flowers, made with precision.

7.24.3.en: The base was not only a flat board (v. 35) but in the form of a cart with four sides (like a handcart). The four side boards were adorned with the same drawings and wreaths.

7.24.4.en: These bases were made so that the lavers would rest upon them, and they were adorned with these shapes to declare God's authority over creation, such as the wild beasts, represented by the lions, the cattle, represented by the oxen, and the plants, represented by the flowers, and also over the heavenly beings, represented by the cherubim. They also declare that these sacrifices, which would be washed in these lavers, are offered for the purification of man and of all creation, so that everything may be clean and man's eyes may be lifted to heaven where the cherubim are. And also by these bloods we satisfy the justice of God, which the cherubim represent. The blood of animals is a type of the blood of Christ the Savior.

7.25.1.en: Axletrees: a bronze rod that is the axis joining the two wheels, around which they turn.

7.25.2.en: Their feet: legs that come down from the four corners of the board of the base.

7.25.3.en: Undersetters: plural of shoulder, a reinforcement of the four corners of the board, rising upward to support the laver from its four sides and coming downward to form four legs of the base.

7.25.4.en: The four shoulders at the corners of the board of the base rose upward so that the laver would rest on them, and the extension of the shoulders downward formed four legs connected to the four wheels, and every two wheels turn around an axle to move the base with the laver when needed.

7.25.5.en: Beside the shoulders hung wreaths of flowers. And the base with everything in it was cast of bronze as one piece, to be solid.

7.26.0.en: Its mouth: a round opening in the center of the panel, a cubit in diameter.

7.26.1.en: The crown: a projection surrounding the opening, whose thickness was four cubits.

7.26.2.en: The board of the base was square, each side four cubits long (two meters), and in its center an opening was made, a cubit in diameter, surrounded by a frame, raised around the opening, and its thickness was a quarter of a cubit, so that the diameter of the opening and its frame was a cubit and a half. And because the board of the base was domed, as will come in (v. 35), it is mentioned here that the opening and its frame were raised.

7.26.3.en: On the crown surrounding its mouth were carvings like the carvings found in (v. 29).

7.27.0.en: Hooks: plural of hook, a curved piece of bronze.

7.27.1.en: The four legs of the base were joined to four hooks to connect to the four wheels. The diameter of the wheel was a cubit and a half (75 cm).

7.28.0.en: Their felloes: the outer rim of the wheel.

7.28.1.en: Their spokes: the wires or rods that connect the outer rim to the center of the wheel. Their naves: the circle in the center of the wheel, joined to the outer rim by the wires, through which passes the axle, or rod, that connects it to the opposite wheel.

7.28.2.en: The wheels were cast with all their parts, the rims, hooks, spokes, and naves, of bronze.

7.29.0.en: The four corners of the base had shoulders cast with the base and not attached to it, for increased strength (as came before in v. 30).

7.30.0.en: Domed: in the shape of a dome.

7.30.1.en: The upper board of the base was not flat but domed, and the height of the highest point of the dome was half a cubit, that is, 25 cm, and the base had hands for pulling it, cast of bronze with the base on its four sides as one part.

7.31.0.en: He carved cherubim, lions, palm trees, and wreaths of flowers on the handles and on the boards of the base, as far as there was room.

7.32.0.en: The ten bases were all of the same measurements and exactly identical, because they were all cast in succession in one mold.

7.32.1.en: If God cared for all this exactness in the making of the lavers in which the sacrifices of the Old Testament were washed, how much more ought you to be exact in preparing to partake of the Holy Mysteries, that is, of the sacrifice of Christ which gives you salvation, by repentance and confession and attending the Liturgy from its beginning and taking part in it with all your heart.

7.33.0.en: After that he made ten bronze lavers and set them above the ten bases, each laver on a base, and the capacity of each laver was 40 baths of water, and the diameter of the laver was two meters; this diameter was at the top, while at the bottom it was less than this so as to enter the opening in the base and remain in the base. There is another opinion, that the four cubits is the height of the laver and not its diameter (see the picture of the laver and the base at the end of the book).

7.34.0.en: Five bases were placed on the right side of the house, that is, toward the south, and five bases on the left side, that is, in the north, and the bronze sea was placed on the southeast of the house.

7.35.0.en: The shovels: plural of shovel, which is the scoop.

7.35.1.en: The basons: a bason is a hollow vessel used for sprinkling water or blood during the rites. Hiram and the team of skilled workers with him made the lavers, the shovels, and the instruments for sprinkling water, and he also completed all the requirements of the Temple as King Solomon decided for the house of the Lord.

7.36.0.en: The pots: vessels for cooking meat.

7.36.2.en: In these five verses is a list of the things Hiram made, and they are:

7.36.4.en: The two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of both pillars

7.36.5.en: The network covering the capital on both pillars

7.36.6.en: The four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network

7.36.7.en: The ten lavers and their movable bases.

7.36.8.en: The sea and the twelve oxen under it

7.36.9.en: The pots, the shovels, and the basons.

7.36.10.en: All of the above was made of bright bronze.

7.36.11.en: Solomon took care to do all the bronze works for the Temple of God with exactness. And God took care in the creation of your body with all precision, because it is a temple for His Holy Spirit, so whenever you move or breathe, thank God and keep your body pure and all your senses, so that the temple of God - which is your body - is fit for His dwelling.

7.37.0.en: The plain: a plain, or valley, that is, a low place.

7.37.1.en: Succoth: it lies east of the Jordan River at a distance of three miles.

7.37.2.en: Zarthan: it lies west of the Jordan River.

7.37.3.en: All the works of casting the preceding equipment and furnishings were done in the plain of the Jordan, in the area lying between Succoth, which lies east of the Jordan River, and Zarthan, which lies west of it, and which was called the land of clay because it is rich in the sand used in making the molds for casting the bronze equipment. Solomon intended that the casting of the bronze be done away from the area of the building of the Temple, so that it would be done with a precision suited to metalwork, and so that there would be no noise at the place of the Temple.

7.37.4.en: If the Temple is a type of the Kingdom, then the foundries are a type of the trials we meet on earth, because metals are cast by fire, and after the vessels are prepared with precision and are beautiful, they enter the Temple; so we, after being tested by trials, enter the Kingdom of Heaven.

7.38.0.en: Because of the multitude of the bronze works and the quantities of bronze used in them, Solomon could not count them exactly, and this shows:

7.38.1.en: 1- That David had prepared large quantities of bronze.

7.38.2.en: 2- Solomon supplemented these quantities generously, out of honor and care for the house of the Lord.

7.39.0.en: The flowers: shapes of flowers of gold on the head of the seven branches of each of the ten golden lampstands inside the house.

7.39.1.en: The lamps: a small vessel that is part of the lampstand, in which the oil and the wick are put to give light.

7.39.2.en: The tongs: plural of tongs, used to lift the used wicks and to put new wicks in the lampstands. The bowls: plural of bowl, that is, basin, used as a vessel for oil.

7.39.3.en: The snuffers: a tool like scissors for cutting off the burnt part of the wick.

7.39.4.en: The spoons: small dishes in which incense is put or in which fire is carried to the lampstands. The censers: plural of censer, that is, the shurriya.

7.39.5.en: The hinges: the hinges in the doors.

7.39.6.en: Solomon also took care of the golden vessels inside the house, that is, the Holy Place, and they are:

7.39.7.en: 1- The altar of incense or the golden altar, which he made of stone and covered with cedar wood and then covered the wood with gold (ch. 6:20-22).

7.39.9.en: 3- Ten golden lampstands, five placed on the right of the house and five on its left before the Holy of Holies, that is, the oracle; and he made the flowers and the lamps that were on the lampstands all of gold.

7.39.10.en: 4- The utensils used in the Holy Place such as the tongs, the bowls, the snuffers, the basons, the spoons, and the censers.

7.39.11.en: 5- The hinges in the doors of the house and the oracle, that is, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

7.39.12.en: It is noticed here that there were ten lampstands in the house, while in the tabernacle of meeting there was one lampstand (Ex 25:31). We also see that the altar of incense was made in the house of stone and covered with wood and gold, while in the tabernacle of meeting it was of wood covered with gold to make it easy to carry. And Solomon made the golden vessels of the house of the Lord by others than Hiram, who was a specialist in bronze work.

7.40.0.en: The vessels: the golden vessels that David won in his victories over the surrounding peoples.

7.40.1.en: All the requirements of the Temple and its building were supplied through King Solomon, who took all the gold and silver his father had prepared, which exceeded the need of the work of building the Temple, and put it in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and did not use it in his palace. David had taken care to collect the silver and gold which he took as spoils in his military victories over the countries surrounding him and had set it all apart for the building of the house of the Lord (2 Sam 8:9-11).

7.40.2.en: Solomon's care in building the Temple of the Lord urges us each to seek how to build within himself a dwelling for God, so that our bodies may be temples of God in which the Holy Spirit dwells, as St. Paul the Apostle called us to do (1 Cor 3:16). The dedication of the Temple (1) The transfer of the ark to the Temple (vv. 1-11:)

7.40.3.en: 1- Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David, which is Zion. 2- And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto king Solomon at the feast in the month Ethanim, which is the seventh month. 3- And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark. 4- And they brought up the ark of the LORD, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle, even those did the priests and the Levites bring up. 5- And king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel, that were assembled unto him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be told nor numbered for multitude.

7.40.4.en: 6- And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the LORD unto his place, into the oracle of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubims.

7.40.5.en: 7- For the cherubims spread forth their two wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubims covered the ark and the staves thereof above.

7.40.6.en: 8- And they drew out the staves, that the ends of the staves were seen out in the holy place before the oracle, and they were not seen without: and there they are unto this day. 9- There was nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt. 10- And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD, 11- So that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD.
